svg.title: Sphere impostor geometry and shading
svg.desc: Ray-sphere geometry of a shaded impostor and the literal pixels of a 20 pixel sphere shaded by the implemented light.
svg.text: a sphere is a disc plus an analytic normal
Frame::ball and ball_fragment: no mesh, one square root per covered pixel
slice through the centre (n_y = 0), looking along the depth axis
d = n_x^2 + n_y^2 covered if d <= 1
n_z = sqrt(1 - d) the near root of the ray-sphere quadratic
normal = (n_x, n_y, n_z) unit length, since d + n_z^2 = 1
depth = cz + n_z * R R is the world radius, r the pixel radius
The silhouette is a circle of r pixels but the depth bulge is R world units, so the
impostor is a sphere only where r = R * zoom * SCALE (Frame::world_sphere); Frame::sphere
draws r = max(R * zoom, 3.5), about 18% smaller, which the views' spacing was tuned with.
the pixels of a sphere with r = 20, sampled at integer coordinates
in (x right, y down, z to viewer);
